title: Zero-to-Instrumented Demo Flow — Lab Notebook (draft)
summary: Working notes for a compact lab that takes a developer from zero to a minimal demo app instrumented with SDK telemetry and Redwood Console hooks. Emphasis on low-friction onboarding, clear event semantics, and token-level cost signals.
motivation: We need a tiny reproducible path that SDK consumers can follow to build confidence: create a client, send a generation, observe token and latency telemetry, add a simple cache, and run a smoke CI. This doc will be the basis for a 30–45 minute hands-on lab and accompanying quickstart markdown.
goals: Produce a 30-minute lab that finishes with an instrumented demo visible in Redwood Console
Demonstrate token-level cost attribution and latency histograms from the SDK
Show a minimal local dev loop (replayable inputs, deterministic seeds)
Surface common failure modes and quick fixes for first-time integrators
components: Tiny demo app (Flask/Express) with one /chat endpoint
SDK client initialization with telemetry hooks
Lightweight in-process cache (LRU) to illustrate batching/caching benefit
Local infra: docker-compose for Redis optional, dev proxy to Redwood hosted API
CI smoke test that runs a single generation and asserts response schema
Instructions to view events/metrics in Redwood Console (route/model dashboards)
flow_steps: 1) Prereqs: git, python/node, docker optional, REDWOOD_API_KEY. Quick check command included.
2) Clone starter repo and open quickstart/ directory. Explain file layout.
3) Install SDK and start local dev server (one command). Provide exact CLI for both Python and Node variants.
4) Initialize client: show environment-driven pattern (REDWOOD_API_KEY), enable telemetry with a sample rate for lab (10%).
5) Send first generation: record token count, latency; emit structured event 'demo.generation' with metadata (route, model, prompt_hash).
6) Flip on local cache and rerun to show reduced token/latency metrics; take screenshot instructions for the Console.
7) Add an error handler to catch and log common API errors (429, 5xx), demonstrate retry/backoff snippet.
8) Run CI smoke: run replay script that hits /chat with sample prompts; assert response contains expected keys and metric events were emitted (local assertions).
9) Optional: enable sampling to only send telemetry for 10% of requests and show how sampling appears in Console counts.
10) Wrap-up: checklist for moving demo to internal demo env or sharing with sales/solutions engineering
sample_config_snippet:
# example (Python)
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-demo-xxx
# minimal client init with telemetry
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), telemetry={'enabled': True, 'sample_rate': 0.1, 'service': 'demo-lab'})

# emit a lightweight event when sending generation
event_payload = {
  'type': 'generation.request',
  'route': '/chat',
  'model': 'redwood/text-1.0',
  'prompt_hash': 'sha1:' + sha1(prompt.encode()).hexdigest()
}
client.telemetry.emit('demo.generation', event_payload)

# call generation (pseudo)
resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=128)
# record token/latency counters in telemetry hooks automatically
metrics_to_collect: latency buckets: p50, p90, p99 (total and server-only if available)
telemetry sampling rate observed vs configured
cache hits vs misses and effect on token counts
runbook_quick_fixes: Auth errors: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY present and not expired; show curl test to verify key access
429s: show backoff snippet + recommend exponential backoff with jitter and token-window smoothing
High latency: toggle smaller model variant (route-based fallback) and measure p50 improvement
Missing telemetry: confirm telemetry.enabled true and network egress allowed from dev machine to telemetry endpoint
Noise in token counts: normalize by prompt templating (strip debug text) and compare hashes
